lines.text: Her beloved knocks at night, his head drenched with dew, and she wonders if she must put her robe back on.
She rises to open the door, her fingers dripping with myrrh, but her beloved has turned and gone.
The watchmen beat her and take her cloak, and she asks the daughters of Jerusalem to tell him she is sick with hunger.
She describes him as outstanding among ten thousand, with a head of purest gold and legs like pillars of marble on bases of silver.
She tells the daughters he has gone down to his garden, and she says she belongs to her beloved.
